competitive_landscape: A fragmented operator base runs the inter-island lancha network — no premium / electric / foiling tier exists. Avianca / Latam serve the air spoke from Quito and Guayaquil. Aggressive National Park controls on operator count, vessel registration and emissions favour a clean entrant — and may actively constrain new diesel operators.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the Baltra↔Puerto Ayora transfer (~30 nm) and the local research/scientific transfers around Academy Bay — inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on protected lee water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: N35 Shuttle is the right platform for the inter-island commuter spine — Santa Cruz↔San Cristóbal (~40 nm) and Santa Cruz↔Isabela (~50 nm). Hybrid Quanta-LR is the longer-horizon Galápagos↔mainland Ecuador trunk (~600 nm) with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the dense inter-island electrification playbook the Galápagos spine can reproduce under an even more aggressive regulatory tailwind.

regulatory_note: Galápagos National Park (DPNG) and Ministerio del Ambiente y Agua tightly regulate every vessel operating in the archipelago: operator licences are capped, vessel categories are fixed, and emissions / wake / wildlife-interaction rules are strict. Active policy direction toward electrification of inter-island transport. UNESCO World Heritage marine reserve since 2001 (original WHS 1978). Ecuador is a MARPOL signatory.
seasonality: Year-round operability; cool/dry season (June–November) brings stronger SE trades and more chop on the inter-island legs — foiling materially outperforms displacement here. Warm/wet season (December–May) is calmer and visitor-peak.
signature_routes: Puerto Ayora ↔ Puerto Baquerizo Moreno (N35 Shuttle)
Baltra Airport ↔ Puerto Ayora silent transfer (Pioneer II)
summary: Santa Cruz (Puerto Ayora) is the tourism epicentre and population hub of the Galápagos and the centre of the inter-island 'lancha' speedboat network linking Santa Cruz with San Cristóbal and Isabela (~40–50 nm legs, ~2 hr each on conventional diesel). The conservation and emissions regime is the most aggressive decarbonisation tailwind in the whole Navier backlog: the Galápagos is a UNESCO World Heritage marine reserve with active pressure from the Galápagos National Park and the Ministerio del Ambiente to electrify diesel inter-island transport. ~270k visitors/yr give real demand; incumbent lanchas are diesel, slow and rough — a silent foiling shuttle is a clean upgrade with a regulatory tailwind few other corridors match.
tagline: The most aggressive decarbonisation tailwind in the whole backlog — a UNESCO marine reserve actively pushing to electrify diesel inter-island transport.
